vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: kubernetes
Version: 1.0.6

The skill bundle is a comprehensive and well-documented platform engineering suite for Kubernetes and OpenShift management. It features a sophisticated multi-agent coordination system with explicit roles, persistent state tracking (via WORKING.md and SESSION.md), and mandatory human-in-the-loop guardrails for all destructive or production-altering actions (defined in AGENTS.md and QUICKREF.md). While some scripts contain potential shell injection vulnerabilities due to the use of 'eval' for constructing curl commands (e.g., in metric-query.sh and log-search.sh), these appear to be unintentional coding flaws rather than evidence of malice. The bundle includes a robust SECURITY.md policy and utility scripts for binary verification, indicating a strong focus on operational safety.

llm.summary: The skill's declared metadata, runtime instructions, and included files are functionally coherent with a Kubernetes multi-agent toolkit, but there are notable inconsistencies and operational risks you should understand before installing.

dimensions.detail: The skill claims to be an instruction-only skill in registry metadata (no install spec, no required env vars) but the included SKILL.md and many scripts clearly require cluster credentials (KUBECONFIG), many CLI binaries (kubectl, oc, helm, kustomize, jq, curl, git) and optional cloud/provider tokens. The code and scripts in the package match the stated purpose (cluster ops, GitOps, security, observability), but the mismatch between registry-level requirements and the SKILL.md/scripts is an incoherence that can lead to surprise privileges during install/use.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md gives explicit runtime instructions that are within scope for a Kubernetes platform agent (read cluster state, apply manifests, run scans, generate SBOMs, create PRs). It explicitly instructs to clone/run third‑party scripts and to require KUBECONFIG and other optional tokens. It warns that destructive scripts exist and that human approval is required for production actions — but this human-approval is a procedural control (not technically enforced by the scripts). The instructions also direct agents to write/update repository files (LOGS.md, MEMORY.md, etc.) which increases persistence of agent actions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no formal install spec in the registry metadata, yet SKILL.md and README recommend cloning a GitHub repo or using 'npx skills add' which will download and place many executable bash scripts onto disk. The SKILL.md points to a third-party GitHub repo (https://github.com/kcns008/cluster-agent-swarm-skills) and explicitly warns to pin to a tag and audit scripts. Downloading and running dozens of scripts from an external repo is higher risk unless you pin/verify checksums; the repository is the apparent install source but the skill package metadata did not declare an install mechanism consistently.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The environment and credential requests in the SKILL.md (KUBECONFIG required; optional AWS/Azure/GCP creds; ArgoCD, Vault, GitHub tokens) are all reasonable for the claimed capabilities. However, the package-level metadata lists no required env vars or credentials, which is inconsistent. Expect to provide sensitive credentials for full functionality; ensure you follow least-privilege practices (namespace-limited service accounts, narrow-scope cloud/service tokens).
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Agents and scripts intentionally persist state into repository files (LOGS.md, MEMORY.md, INCIDENTS.md, create PRs via skill-improvement-pr.sh). That behavior is coherent with an orchestrator but increases blast radius: the skill may need write access to the working repository and optional tokens (e.g., GitHub) to create PRs. always:false is correct (no forced inclusion). Verify that any human-approval gate is enforced by your platform rather than relying solely on the skill's procedural warnings.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package appears to implement a realistic Kubernetes multi-agent toolkit, but there are packaging and operational red flags you should address before installing: 1) Metadata mismatch — the registry entry claims 'instruction-only' and 'no required env vars' while SKILL.md and included scripts require KUBECONFIG and many CLIs; confirm which is authoritative. 2) Audit before running — clone the referenced GitHub repo and review scripts locally; do not run curl|bash or unpinned installs. Pin to a specific tag/commit and verify checksums if you download binaries. 3) Least privilege only — create namespace-scoped service accounts and minimal cloud roles; never hand over owner/root credentials. 4) Limit tokens — if you provide a GITHUB_TOKEN or ARGOCD token, scope it narrowly (repo write only where necessary) and prefer offline/manual PRs for production changes. 5) Sandbox first — run the skill in an isolated test cluster and verify the human-approval workflow is enforced by your platform (do not rely on the skill to self-enforce). 6) Verify persistence and repo access — decide whether you are comfortable giving the agent ability to write LOGS.md, MEMORY.md, or create PRs; if not, remove/lock those capabilities or use read-only tokens. If you need to proceed, pin to a verified release, audit the scripts, and restrict credentials to the minimum required. If anything in the repository is unexpected (hidden endpoints, network exfiltration, or undocumented remote downloads), do not install and report to your security team.
